newsitem.title: USA: Matav says Israel mandates cable extension.
newsitem.headline: Matav says Israel mandates cable extension.

text.p: Matav-Cable Systems Media Ltd said on Monday the Israeli Ministry of Communications will require Israeli cable companies to extend cable television services to peripheral geographical areas.
Matav said it was disappointed with the decision and was considering a legal challenge. The decision was made by the ministry's exceptional cases committee, it said.
Matav said it was impossible to know the financial impact.
The company also said it was investigating various ways of complying with the ruling, including delivering services through underground cabling or direct broadcast satellite.
Matav also said an Israeli court denied a motion from a rival group which challenged Barak Group's election as the second licensee of international telephone service in Israel.
Barak is made up of Matav Cable, Clal Industries unit Clalcom, Sprint Corp, Deutsche Telecom and France Telecom, it said in a separate statement.

The decision cleared the way for the Barak Group to prepare to implement its proposed international telephone service, the company said. The group was originally notified of the award in November, Matav said.
Robert Avi-Tal, president and chief executive officer of Matav said: "With this challenge behind us, we are ready to begin implementing this new international telephone service."
He said while the rival Dolphin Group could still appeal the District Court's decision, the company felt it could begin preparations to implement the service.
Matav is an operator and provider of broadband cable television services in Israel.
